https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgDuHDrZ_eU

值得閱讀的理由

  • 透過實際操作，呈現這台復古造型相機如何在吸睛設計與笨拙體驗之間形成反差。
  • 介紹跨越不同年代的影像濾鏡，以及它們帶來的特色與意外缺陷。
  • 說明即拍列印、影片 QR 碼與手機 App 等功能的巧思，也揭露使用限制。
  • 以幽默而直白的試用心得，思考一台相機功能很多，是否就能成為真正好用的全能相機。

摘要

復古外型與不太順手的操作

Cherry 試用 2026 年推出的 Fuji miniEvo Cinema，這款相機重現富士早期電影攝影機 Single-8 的外觀，配有直立握把、光學取景器與皮套，並結合即拍列印與影片拍攝。握持時，手指似乎能自然地找到快門與控制鍵，但實際操作卻不如外型看來俐落：開機到拍下第一張照片約需十秒，拍影片還得先切換模式，再按住按鈕開始錄影，每段最長僅十五秒。

年代濾鏡的魅力與失誤

相機最有趣的功能，是轉盤上的十種年代濾鏡，從 1930 年代一路涵蓋至 2020 年代。不同設定分別模擬默片黑白影像、老式 CRT 電視掃描線、CCD 與 DV 攝影機，甚至重現 YouTube 畫面介面。不過，有些濾鏡會把格線直接印進影像，讓人物臉上出現不該有的線條；相機也會在晃動時加入特效。Cherry 認為，這些復古效果用來拍攝現代景物頗有趣味，卻也顯示設計並非處處周到。

變焦、即拍列印與 QR 碼巧思

鏡頭環調整的不是焦距，而是濾鏡強度；真正的變焦則由另一個撥桿控制，而且是分段變焦，短短十五秒的影片可能有不少時間耗在拉近、拉遠上。作為即拍相機，它能將影像列印成方形相片，也能從一段影片中挑出單格輸出；Cherry 發現，實際列印的照片甚至比相機預覽看起來清晰。列印影片畫面時，相片角落會附上 QR 碼，掃描後即可觀看影片，但富士伺服器只會保存內容兩年，期限過後影片去向令人擔憂。

手機連線與儲存上的限制

手機 App 可提供即時預覽與遙控拍攝，卻沒有直接把原始照片或影片傳到手機的功能；Cherry 原先只能靠截圖或錄製螢幕保存內容，還得另外裁掉介面。後來他找到一個迂迴方法：先列印照片，預覽畫面出現相框與儲存按鈕後，便能把影像存進手機。照片與影片也可存入 TF 記憶卡，但隨附讀卡器在日常使用中竟然裂開，與套件內質感出色的皮套形成反差。

有創意，卻難以成為全能相機

Cherry 原以為，能先預覽再列印、套用年代濾鏡又能拍影片的相機，或許會是理想的全能機種；實際用過後，他卻覺得每項功能都有些彆扭，彼此加在一起也沒有讓體驗變得更完整。miniEvo Cinema 概念大膽、玩法獨特，卻未能把核心功能做好，反而常妨礙使用者完成其他操作。影片最後，Cherry 邀請觀眾分享看法，並為影片按讚、訂閱與開啟通知。

================================================

As we all know, anything that looks like this must be a movie camera. It has a vertical pistol-grip, an optical viewfinder, and a leather holster. This is the Fuji miniEvo Cinema, released in 2026 a recreation of Fuji's very first film movie camera, the Single-8, and it's an instant film movie camera. It's been a long time since I've picked up a camera and had no idea where to start. I'm so used to triple-lens setups, 200MP sensors, and computational photography. Seeing this old-school beast feels oddly unfamiliar. Grab the grip, and it clicks. Your index finger rests naturally on the shutter button,.

while your thumb can reach all the front controls. Your left hand isn't idle either; it operates all the buttons on the left side. Speaking of which, I've got it all figured out now. This is so good to use or so I thought. It's actually really awkward. Imagine you're a cowboy, drawing this camera. From power-on to capturing your first shot takes a full ten seconds. I almost thought people back in the 60s had it good, but instead, it's sending me back to the stone age.

Some of you might say: "Come on, it says Cinema right in the name. It's for video. You can't expect it to snap street candid shots instantly." Fair enough, let's try shooting video. Anyone who's used the WeChat camera knows: tap briefly for a photo, hold down for video. Should be easy, right? Not quite. You first have to toggle the switch here, then hold to start recording. Each clip can run up to 15 seconds. You can record a short clip, release, then record another. The in-camera preview stitches them together into one video, but the files stay separate very purist. You can also attach this magnetic magnifier,.

which lets you see down to the pixel level. It works brilliantly. The shutter button has an extremely light touch with almost no tactile feedback. It's easy to over-press it by accident. But if you apply just the right amount of pressure, it can even lock onto faces. It can track a face that you can barely make out at the pixel level. So with this clunky handling and hardware, what's the point of this camera? Sometimes you just need to look at what's right in front of you. Looking over the whole body, the largest component isn't the lens or the screen it's this dial.

That's the most fun part of the miniEvo Cinema. It cycles through 10 era-based filters spanning from the 1930s to the 2020s. Let's switch to one and see. Hold on please each filter has its own theme. The 1930s setting mimics silent black-and-white motion picture film, giving that classic Chaplin vibe. Though Fuji wasn't fully consistent here this filter still has audio. The 1970s setting gives you those scanlines, the look of old bulky CRT televisions. 2000s is that beloved.

CCD and DV camcorder aesthetic. The most amusing one is 2010s: it replicates the look of YouTube video, even burning in the on-screen UI. Now guess what the newest one, the 2020s preset, gives you? The answer: nothing at all. Or at least that's what I thought at first until I took photos with a friend. I picked the sharpest era preset hoping for a cleaner shot. When I reviewed it, I went: why is there a line across my face? Turns out that grid isn't just an overlay guide; it's burned into the frame. Oh no, that's a problem. And it's not just this one. The 2000, 1940 and 1930.

presets slap those marks right over your subject. I love using vintage filters to shoot modern scenes. People from those eras would never have ridden a subway, right? Back in the 90s, Shenzhen's Minghua Ship was still out on the water; now it sits surrounded by a dense cluster of buildings. It also adds special effects when the camera shakes. If you've followed this far, you get how wild its concept is. Now, how would you zoom? Twist the lens ring and yes, it does turn, but it only adjusts filter intensity.

The real zoom control is this lever. The zoom steps are incremental, so out of that already-short 15-second clip, you can easily waste half just zooming in and out. Wait a second. Does anyone remember this is an instant camera? Its square body fits instant film perfectly. Up top you've got the flash and selfie mirror, just like a regular instax. Shoot, trigger it, and out pops a print. But its thickness gives away how it works: fundamentally, it's a printer. That opens up more creative tricks. You can print just the best frame from a sequence,.

or output images that you'd never expect to see on instant film. Thanks to its 1/5-inch sensor, the printed photo comes out noticeably sharper than what you see on the camera's preview. How do you print? My favourite button: pull it out, then rotate it half a turn. That sound is so satisfying, just like a gashapon capsule machine. Two full rotations, and your photo ejects. Has anyone spotted the clever little detail? We've talked about video and instant prints of live photos, but this isn't magic. The simple.

solution: QR codes. If you print a video still, a QR code appears in the corner of the print. Grab your phone, scan it, and you can watch the video. Here's the bigger catch. Squinting at the fine print on Fuji's website with my less-than-perfect vision, I found out their servers only keep the content for two years. What happens after those two years? My videos gone? What if I don't print the photos and videos and just export them instead? That's not an option either. The phone app, likely tuned to match the camera's glacial processing speed, forces an opening animation first.

After that, you can preview the live view and trigger shots remotely. That part is handy, but there is no button to transfer the actual files to your phone. Want a photo? Take a screenshot. Want the video? Screen-record it. And don't forget to crop out the UI borders. I just found a trick to save photos to your phone. Look: right now, there's no way to save this image. But you can print it first. OK Once printed, you'll see a frame appear on the preview, and then, along with a save button.

Pick any shot, and now you can save it to your phone. Got it? As a photographer, of course I bring a memory card. Photos and videos are stored on the TF card, and the card is mine. The Creator Kit does come with a nicely finished card reader it even feels better built than the camera itself. Mine cracked just from regular use. The kit also includes that leather holster I showed at the start. It's such a premium piece, it almost feels like you're buying the case and getting the camera as a bonus. All in all, the miniEvo Cinema is a hard camera to sum up. I once thought an instant camera combining preview-before-print,.

era filters and video recording would be the ultimate all-in-one, the only camera I'd ever need. In reality, every function is odd on its own, and together they feel like the ultrahand builds from "Tears of the Kingdom". It doesn't nail its core job, and it gets in the way of everything else. What do you think of this camera? Alright, that wraps up this video. If you enjoyed it, please hit like, subscribe and turn on notifications it means a lot to me. This is Cherry and I'll see you next time. Bye!

Cherry 試用 2026 年推出的 Fuji miniEvo Cinema，這款相機重現富士早期電影攝影機 Single-8 的外觀，配有直立握把、光學取景器與皮套，並結合即拍列印與影片拍攝。握持時，手指似乎能自然地找到快門與控制鍵，但實際操作卻不如外型看來俐落：開機到拍下第一張照片約需十秒，拍影片還得先切換模式，再按住按鈕開始錄影，每段最長僅十五秒。

年代濾鏡的魅力與失誤

相機最有趣的功能，是轉盤上的十種年代濾鏡，從 1930 年代一路涵蓋至 2020 年代。不同設定分別模擬默片黑白影像、老式 CRT 電視掃描線、CCD 與 DV 攝影機，甚至重現 YouTube 畫面介面。不過，有些濾鏡會把格線直接印進影像，讓人物臉上出現不該有的線條；相機也會在晃動時加入特效。Cherry 認為，這些復古效果用來拍攝現代景物頗有趣味，卻也顯示設計並非處處周到。

變焦、即拍列印與 QR 碼巧思

鏡頭環調整的不是焦距，而是濾鏡強度；真正的變焦則由另一個撥桿控制，而且是分段變焦，短短十五秒的影片可能有不少時間耗在拉近、拉遠上。作為即拍相機，它能將影像列印成方形相片，也能從一段影片中挑出單格輸出；Cherry 發現，實際列印的照片甚至比相機預覽看起來清晰。列印影片畫面時，相片角落會附上 QR 碼，掃描後即可觀看影片，但富士伺服器只會保存內容兩年，期限過後影片去向令人擔憂。

手機連線與儲存上的限制

手機 App 可提供即時預覽與遙控拍攝，卻沒有直接把原始照片或影片傳到手機的功能；Cherry 原先只能靠截圖或錄製螢幕保存內容，還得另外裁掉介面。後來他找到一個迂迴方法：先列印照片，預覽畫面出現相框與儲存按鈕後，便能把影像存進手機。照片與影片也可存入 TF 記憶卡，但隨附讀卡器在日常使用中竟然裂開，與套件內質感出色的皮套形成反差。

有創意，卻難以成為全能相機

Cherry 原以為，能先預覽再列印、套用年代濾鏡又能拍影片的相機，或許會是理想的全能機種；實際用過後，他卻覺得每項功能都有些彆扭，彼此加在一起也沒有讓體驗變得更完整。miniEvo Cinema 概念大膽、玩法獨特，卻未能把核心功能做好，反而常妨礙使用者完成其他操作。影片最後，Cherry 邀請觀眾分享看法，並為影片按讚、訂閱與開啟通知。

================================================

As we all know, anything that looks like this must be a movie camera. It has a vertical pistol-grip, an optical viewfinder, and a leather holster. This is the Fuji miniEvo Cinema, released in 2026 a recreation of Fuji's very first film movie camera, the Single-8, and it's an instant film movie camera. It's been a long time since I've picked up a camera and had no idea where to start. I'm so used to triple-lens setups, 200MP sensors, and computational photography. Seeing this old-school beast feels oddly unfamiliar. Grab the grip, and it clicks. Your index finger rests naturally on the shutter button,.

while your thumb can reach all the front controls. Your left hand isn't idle either; it operates all the buttons on the left side. Speaking of which, I've got it all figured out now. This is so good to use or so I thought. It's actually really awkward. Imagine you're a cowboy, drawing this camera. From power-on to capturing your first shot takes a full ten seconds. I almost thought people back in the 60s had it good, but instead, it's sending me back to the stone age.

Some of you might say: "Come on, it says Cinema right in the name. It's for video. You can't expect it to snap street candid shots instantly." Fair enough, let's try shooting video. Anyone who's used the WeChat camera knows: tap briefly for a photo, hold down for video. Should be easy, right? Not quite. You first have to toggle the switch here, then hold to start recording. Each clip can run up to 15 seconds. You can record a short clip, release, then record another. The in-camera preview stitches them together into one video, but the files stay separate very purist. You can also attach this magnetic magnifier,.

which lets you see down to the pixel level. It works brilliantly. The shutter button has an extremely light touch with almost no tactile feedback. It's easy to over-press it by accident. But if you apply just the right amount of pressure, it can even lock onto faces. It can track a face that you can barely make out at the pixel level. So with this clunky handling and hardware, what's the point of this camera? Sometimes you just need to look at what's right in front of you. Looking over the whole body, the largest component isn't the lens or the screen it's this dial.

That's the most fun part of the miniEvo Cinema. It cycles through 10 era-based filters spanning from the 1930s to the 2020s. Let's switch to one and see. Hold on please each filter has its own theme. The 1930s setting mimics silent black-and-white motion picture film, giving that classic Chaplin vibe. Though Fuji wasn't fully consistent here this filter still has audio. The 1970s setting gives you those scanlines, the look of old bulky CRT televisions. 2000s is that beloved.

CCD and DV camcorder aesthetic. The most amusing one is 2010s: it replicates the look of YouTube video, even burning in the on-screen UI. Now guess what the newest one, the 2020s preset, gives you? The answer: nothing at all. Or at least that's what I thought at first until I took photos with a friend. I picked the sharpest era preset hoping for a cleaner shot. When I reviewed it, I went: why is there a line across my face? Turns out that grid isn't just an overlay guide; it's burned into the frame. Oh no, that's a problem. And it's not just this one. The 2000, 1940 and 1930.

presets slap those marks right over your subject. I love using vintage filters to shoot modern scenes. People from those eras would never have ridden a subway, right? Back in the 90s, Shenzhen's Minghua Ship was still out on the water; now it sits surrounded by a dense cluster of buildings. It also adds special effects when the camera shakes. If you've followed this far, you get how wild its concept is. Now, how would you zoom? Twist the lens ring and yes, it does turn, but it only adjusts filter intensity.

The real zoom control is this lever. The zoom steps are incremental, so out of that already-short 15-second clip, you can easily waste half just zooming in and out. Wait a second. Does anyone remember this is an instant camera? Its square body fits instant film perfectly. Up top you've got the flash and selfie mirror, just like a regular instax. Shoot, trigger it, and out pops a print. But its thickness gives away how it works: fundamentally, it's a printer. That opens up more creative tricks. You can print just the best frame from a sequence,.

or output images that you'd never expect to see on instant film. Thanks to its 1/5-inch sensor, the printed photo comes out noticeably sharper than what you see on the camera's preview. How do you print? My favourite button: pull it out, then rotate it half a turn. That sound is so satisfying, just like a gashapon capsule machine. Two full rotations, and your photo ejects. Has anyone spotted the clever little detail? We've talked about video and instant prints of live photos, but this isn't magic. The simple.

solution: QR codes. If you print a video still, a QR code appears in the corner of the print. Grab your phone, scan it, and you can watch the video. Here's the bigger catch. Squinting at the fine print on Fuji's website with my less-than-perfect vision, I found out their servers only keep the content for two years. What happens after those two years? My videos gone? What if I don't print the photos and videos and just export them instead? That's not an option either. The phone app, likely tuned to match the camera's glacial processing speed, forces an opening animation first.

After that, you can preview the live view and trigger shots remotely. That part is handy, but there is no button to transfer the actual files to your phone. Want a photo? Take a screenshot. Want the video? Screen-record it. And don't forget to crop out the UI borders. I just found a trick to save photos to your phone. Look: right now, there's no way to save this image. But you can print it first. OK Once printed, you'll see a frame appear on the preview, and then, along with a save button.

Pick any shot, and now you can save it to your phone. Got it? As a photographer, of course I bring a memory card. Photos and videos are stored on the TF card, and the card is mine. The Creator Kit does come with a nicely finished card reader it even feels better built than the camera itself. Mine cracked just from regular use. The kit also includes that leather holster I showed at the start. It's such a premium piece, it almost feels like you're buying the case and getting the camera as a bonus. All in all, the miniEvo Cinema is a hard camera to sum up. I once thought an instant camera combining preview-before-print,.

era filters and video recording would be the ultimate all-in-one, the only camera I'd ever need. In reality, every function is odd on its own, and together they feel like the ultrahand builds from "Tears of the Kingdom". It doesn't nail its core job, and it gets in the way of everything else. What do you think of this camera? Alright, that wraps up this video. If you enjoyed it, please hit like, subscribe and turn on notifications it means a lot to me. This is Cherry and I'll see you next time. Bye!

值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現《GTA 6》在畫面、細節與世界規模上的驚人野心，並比較不同主機的遊戲表現。
  • 整理遊戲中豐富的互動設計，從購物、駕車到手機功能，展現開放世界的生活感。
  • 不只稱讚遊戲，也坦率指出 30 FPS 限制與前期劇情節奏緩慢等缺點。

摘要

驚人的規模與明顯限制

作者認為《GTA 6》是遊戲產業的巔峰之作，開發成本估計高達十億至二十億美元，規模之大或許十年內都難有作品超越。不過，遊戲在支援主機上最高僅有30 FPS，激烈戰鬥時甚至可能降至 20 FPS，而且沒有可調整的畫質設定。

作者在解禁後立刻遊玩，連續體驗至天亮。他認為前十小時的劇情只能算尚可，角色間的張力不足，也還沒有令人印象深刻的人物；但有媒體表示後續劇情內容豐富，因此他仍抱持期待。若能接受畫面更新率與前期劇情兩項缺點，遊戲其餘部分展現出的製作水準依然極為出色。

主機效能與視覺表現

作者表示，Xbox Series S 的表現超出預期，幾乎完整支援遊戲功能，甚至具備光線追蹤髮絲效果，只是細節略少、畫面稍軟；以價格和小尺寸螢幕而言，仍能提供完整體驗。PS5 與 Xbox Series X 則以原生 1440P 呈現畫面，街道細節、動態物件與光影效果都十分突出，日出與日落尤其令人驚豔。PS5 Pro 則帶來主機平台中最清晰銳利的視覺體驗，人物肌膚、建材與水面反射均清楚可見。

由於作者難以接受 30 FPS，他以擷取卡搭配影格補間遊玩；他也提到，使用較新的 NVIDIA 顯示卡時，開源專案可提供影格生成與 DLSS 等功能。即使只是開車經過街道或乘船前往任務地點，沿途景色仍讓他不斷感到驚艷。

細節豐富、充滿生活感的開放世界

作者形容《GTA 6》的細節密度是自己玩過的遊戲中最高的。地圖約為《GTA 5》的兩倍，街邊商店各有不同裝潢，不像複製貼上的場景。玩家在超市購物後會拿到實體袋子，得把它放進車尾箱，再帶回住處；長槍則收在車尾箱的武器箱中，取出時還可能引起旁人注意。角色上下車、手持飲料等小動作，也讓世界更具真實感。

角色身材會隨行動改變，鍛鍊可以增加肌肉與健康值。住家裡還有一台名為 JoySystem 的遊戲主機，玩家能玩其中的射擊遊戲。手機功能也比前作更豐富，除了查看社群動態與健身數據，開車時也能傳訊息或看影片。作者遊玩十小時後，探索範圍仍不到地圖十分之一，並表示遇見的數百名 NPC 各有特色，尚未發現重複角色。

駕駛、NPC 與生活成本

作者特別注意到 NPC 駕駛的反應與道路上的各種怪人；他甚至遇上一名坐輪椅的老太太試圖搶劫，自己出手後對方竟又立刻站了起來。駕駛時不宜一路把油門踩到底，PlayStation 控制器的扳機阻力能讓玩家更細膩地控制加速。控制器喇叭還會播放來電鈴聲，也能傳出導航語音，營造手機就在車前引導路線的感覺。

遊戲中的物價也讓作者大感意外：任務報酬可能只有三百美元，家用食物與飲料卻要一百美元，改裝保險桿也得花上數百美元；收費道路、短程計程車與催促司機的費用更高得驚人。作者打趣說，遊戲裡的資本家似乎比黑幫還狠，甚至連通膨都被做進了世界觀。

更守規矩的犯罪與在地化趣味

犯罪的代價也比以往高。遊戲初期不能隨意搶車，角色的臉孔、衣著與座車都可能被記錄；即使遭人搶劫，玩家也不能不加思索地反擊，否則可能引來警方通緝。作者因此覺得本作或許是最講規矩的一代，但 Rockstar 仍試圖在寫實感與遊戲樂趣之間取得平衡。他也提到能免費把車送到玩家身邊的修車店人物，稱對方是 Vice City 的大善人。

遊戲中的在地化內容也令作者發笑，包括女性主角搶劫的銀行名稱、帶有雙關意味的應用程式，以及角色談論風水的橋段。電台甚至收錄了粵語歌曲，讓他格外意外。

慢熱劇情與主機版本細節

儘管世界探索令作者著迷，他仍覺得劇情缺少《GTA 5》那種混亂、自由又令人振奮的氣勢。前十小時大多描寫兩名主角相處與墜入愛河，男主角的個性仍不清楚，故事也沒有充分交代他為何如此愛慕女主角。作者更期待開場就有強烈衝突或出人意料的犯罪事件；目前支撐他繼續遊玩的，主要是探索開放世界的渴望。此外，經典作弊碼要通關後才會解鎖。

在主機表現比較中，Xbox Series S 以 720P 渲染並升頻至 1080P，整體畫面稍顯柔和，但在 24 至 27 吋螢幕上仍能維持完整遊戲體驗。它在髮絲效果與 NPC 數量方面沒有重大妥協，不過水窪與玻璃的反射較簡化，NPC 移動時偶爾會出現殘影，角色皮膚材質也有所縮減。影片字幕在此處中斷，後續版本比較內容未完整呈現。

================================================

GTA 6 is absolutely the pinnacle of the video game industry. I've never played a game built on such a massive scale with this level of detail. It's mind-blowing. The development cost for this entry is estimated at $1–2 billion that's equivalent to thirty Black Myths, or five Cyberpunk 2077 titles. We might not see another game of this scope for the next decade. Let's start with some obvious issues we've found so far. GTA 6 caps out at 30 FPS on the supported consoles, and frame rates can drop to 20 FPS during intense combat sequences. There are no graphical settings to tweak at all. I jumped in as soon as the embargo lifted at 7 PM and played straight through until dawn. Story-wise, the first ten hours are just passable. It lacks the character tension seen in earlier entries; there aren't any standout, memorable characters yet. Outlets that finished the game early say there's plenty more story content later on, so I'm staying hopeful. If you can accept those two caveats, what you're getting is the pinnacle of video game craft GTA 6. I'll run through full, detailed testing in the second half of this video, but for now, let's quickly show you how it actually runs. The Xbox Series S is really pulling its weight. Just like I predicted in my last video, the XSS supports every feature of the game fully. It even has ray-traced hair strands, though there is a slight drop in detail and the image looks a little softer. If you don't have an enormous display, the XSS works perfectly fine. For just 1400 yuan, you can run this game. Rockstar's optimization is nothing short of incredible. The PS5 and Xbox Series X render at 1440P native, with absolutely stellar visuals. This is reportedly the best ray tracing. we've seen in any released game to date. Street environments are incredibly intricate, packed with countless dynamic assets, paired with atmospheric lighting that makes sunrises and sunsets look absolutely breathtaking. If you happen to own a PS5 Pro, congratulations: you're getting the best visual experience ever on a game console. The most powerful console paired with this flagship game delivers crisp, sharp imagery. You can make out skin textures on characters up close, building materials at mid-range, and crystal-clear water reflections. Rockstar says they have squeezed every last bit of performance out of the hardware.

Even when I'm just driving past streets for a mission or boating over to pick up a package, the roadside scenery keeps blowing me away. That said like many of you, I simply cannot stand playing at 30 FPS. I played the whole session with a capture card for frame interpolation. If you have an RTX 40-series or newer NVIDIA GPU, there's an open-source project that comes with frame generation and DLSS 5. It even has a beauty filter if you don't like how the protagonist looks, and the latency stays well within acceptable limits. GTA 6 has the richest detail of any game I've played. On your first playthrough, you will constantly be amazed by all the little touches. The map is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's,. with an astonishing density of detail. The storefronts along the streets feel authentic, and they are not copy-pasted; each one has unique decor and styling, just like the variety of boutique shops you'd find at a tourist spot. Sometimes when I pass a small shop, I genuinely get the urge to walk inside and look around. When you shop at a supermarket now, items no longer vanish into some alternate inventory pocket. You get a physical shopping bag instead. You have to place that bag in your car trunk, then carry the groceries up to your place once you get home. There's even an electronics store--my favorite kind of shop, can you believe it? They sell Beats headphones and phone cases. Hmm, though I wonder who's even going to see those phone cases. If you park in a tight spot, the protagonist will squeeze out sideways. Long guns no longer materialize out of thin air; they live inside a weapons case in the trunk. Pulling one out can attract unwanted attention, so you have to decide whether to carry that long rifle with you when you step out of the vehicle. Drinks you buy are held in either your left or right hand, and you have to set down each hand's items separately. I was blown away the first time I played San Andreas, back when characters could gain weight. Now the player character's physique. also changes based on your actions. Working out builds muscle and raises your health. Your in-game home even has its own game console not a PlayStation, it's called the JoySystem. And that zombie-shooting game on it? It's actually pretty fun. GTA 4 introduced the in-game cellphone, GTA 5 used phones to drive story beats, and in GTA 6, you can even browse a social media feed, check your fitness stats, and so much more. You can also use your phone while driving firing off texts or watching videos. It's one of those little details you really have to experience in GTA 6.

I've put in ten hours, and I've uncovered less than a tenth of the map. I can't even imagine how much more content is still ahead. I've run into hundreds of NPCs so far, and I haven't seen a duplicate. These aren't just procedurally generated mixes; Rockstar actually built tons of unique NPCs, each with their own personality it's insane. Take Jason, the male protagonist's neighbor, for example. You'll hear him every time you pull out of the driveway. Still, the NPC drivers left the biggest impression on me. The acceleration pushback feels so visceral. All I did was tap their car! You also run into all kinds of wild characters out on the road. Once I headed out to buy clothes, and right as I stepped outside, an elderly lady in a wheelchair tried to rob me. I kicked her, and she popped right back up. Total miracle worker, apparently. For driving in this entry, flooring the gas nonstop isn't recommended. If you're using a PlayStation controller, the throttle trigger has a distinct resistance notch. I usually hold the trigger right at that notch. You can also adjust the controller speaker volume in settings I'd recommend cranking it up. When you get an in-game call, the ringtone plays straight from the controller speaker, just like your real phone buzzing in your pocket. You can also route navigation audio to the controller. While driving, it feels like your phone is mounted up front, guiding you and alerting you once you reach your destination. And honestly, it's not just Americans complaining about high costs even I'm blown away by how expensive everything is. The protagonist risks life and limb, and a mission only pays around $300. Groceries and drinks for the family already run me $100. Adding a front bumper for a car modification costs hundreds more. The most absurd part? Toll roads. The electronic toll system charges me $5. Is this capitalism at work? A two-kilometer taxi ride costs $42. Rush the driver, and that's an extra $5. Skip the ride entirely, and they charge $100. Capitalists are even more ruthless than gangsters, if you ask me. Taxis in GTA 5 never cost this much per kilometer.

They even built inflation into the game. The cost of committing crimes has also gone up drastically. The protagonist almost behaves like a law-abiding citizen. Early on, you can't just hijack cars off the street willy-nilly. Your face, outfit and the vehicle you're driving will get flagged. Even if someone tries to rob you, you can't immediately take them out that will also trigger a wanted level. This might be the most rule-following GTA yet. That said, Rockstar stated they wanted to balance gameplay fun and realism. Take Joey, the auto shop guy from Lantos Reef, the strongest NPC in the whole game. He can teleport your car to you for free. A true good samaritan of Vice City. The localization is also wild. The bank the female protagonist robs is called Get Cash Now. Lots of games have scan mechanics, but what on earth is "AI Snoop"? When the protagonist first sets up the family fund, the banking app they hand their cash over to has a very specific name you'll know it if you get the reference. I cracked up when the male lead and his best friend had a whole conversation about feng shui. And get this: the radio even includes Cantonese tracks. Would you believe it? That said, the story just doesn't deliver the same chaotic, liberating rush I got from GTA 5. The pacing is extremely slow-burn. The first ten hours are basically just the two leads playing house and falling in love. Even now, I haven't met a single character that sticks with me. After all this playtime, I still can't pin down the male protagonist's personality all I know is he's head over heels for the female lead. The game doesn't spend much time explaining why, either. 由於作者難以接受 30 FPS，他以擷取卡搭配影格補間遊玩；他也提到，使用較新的 NVIDIA 顯示卡時，開源專案可提供影格生成與 DLSS 等功能。即使只是開車經過街道或乘船前往任務地點，沿途景色仍讓他不斷感到驚艷。

細節豐富、充滿生活感的開放世界

作者形容《GTA 6》的細節密度是自己玩過的遊戲中最高的。地圖約為《GTA 5》的兩倍，街邊商店各有不同裝潢，不像複製貼上的場景。玩家在超市購物後會拿到實體袋子，得把它放進車尾箱，再帶回住處；長槍則收在車尾箱的武器箱中，取出時還可能引起旁人注意。角色上下車、手持飲料等小動作，也讓世界更具真實感。

角色身材會隨行動改變，鍛鍊可以增加肌肉與健康值。住家裡還有一台名為 JoySystem 的遊戲主機，玩家能玩其中的射擊遊戲。手機功能也比前作更豐富，除了查看社群動態與健身數據，開車時也能傳訊息或看影片。作者遊玩十小時後，探索範圍仍不到地圖十分之一，並表示遇見的數百名 NPC 各有特色，尚未發現重複角色。

駕駛、NPC 與生活成本

作者特別注意到 NPC 駕駛的反應與道路上的各種怪人；他甚至遇上一名坐輪椅的老太太試圖搶劫，自己出手後對方竟又立刻站了起來。駕駛時不宜一路把油門踩到底，PlayStation 控制器的扳機阻力能讓玩家更細膩地控制加速。控制器喇叭還會播放來電鈴聲，也能傳出導航語音，營造手機就在車前引導路線的感覺。

遊戲中的物價也讓作者大感意外：任務報酬可能只有三百美元，家用食物與飲料卻要一百美元，改裝保險桿也得花上數百美元；收費道路、短程計程車與催促司機的費用更高得驚人。作者打趣說，遊戲裡的資本家似乎比黑幫還狠，甚至連通膨都被做進了世界觀。

更守規矩的犯罪與在地化趣味

犯罪的代價也比以往高。遊戲初期不能隨意搶車，角色的臉孔、衣著與座車都可能被記錄；即使遭人搶劫，玩家也不能不加思索地反擊，否則可能引來警方通緝。作者因此覺得本作或許是最講規矩的一代，但 Rockstar 仍試圖在寫實感與遊戲樂趣之間取得平衡。他也提到能免費把車送到玩家身邊的修車店人物，稱對方是 Vice City 的大善人。

遊戲中的在地化內容也令作者發笑，包括女性主角搶劫的銀行名稱、帶有雙關意味的應用程式，以及角色談論風水的橋段。電台甚至收錄了粵語歌曲，讓他格外意外。

慢熱劇情與主機版本細節

儘管世界探索令作者著迷，他仍覺得劇情缺少《GTA 5》那種混亂、自由又令人振奮的氣勢。前十小時大多描寫兩名主角相處與墜入愛河，男主角的個性仍不清楚，故事也沒有充分交代他為何如此愛慕女主角。作者更期待開場就有強烈衝突或出人意料的犯罪事件；目前支撐他繼續遊玩的，主要是探索開放世界的渴望。此外，經典作弊碼要通關後才會解鎖。

在主機表現比較中，Xbox Series S 以 720P 渲染並升頻至 1080P，整體畫面稍顯柔和，但在 24 至 27 吋螢幕上仍能維持完整遊戲體驗。它在髮絲效果與 NPC 數量方面沒有重大妥協，不過水窪與玻璃的反射較簡化，NPC 移動時偶爾會出現殘影，角色皮膚材質也有所縮減。影片字幕在此處中斷，後續版本比較內容未完整呈現。

GTA 6 is absolutely the pinnacle of the video game industry. I've never played a game built on such a massive scale with this level of detail. It's mind-blowing. The development cost for this entry is estimated at $1–2 billion that's equivalent to thirty Black Myths, or five Cyberpunk 2077 titles. We might not see another game of this scope for the next decade. Let's start with some obvious issues we've found so far. GTA 6 caps out at 30 FPS on the supported consoles, and frame rates can drop to 20 FPS during intense combat sequences. There are no graphical settings to tweak at all. I jumped in as soon as the embargo lifted at 7 PM and played straight through until dawn. Story-wise, the first ten hours are just passable. It lacks the character tension seen in earlier entries; there aren't any standout, memorable characters yet. Outlets that finished the game early say there's plenty more story content later on, so I'm staying hopeful. If you can accept those two caveats, what you're getting is the pinnacle of video game craft GTA 6. I'll run through full, detailed testing in the second half of this video, but for now, let's quickly show you how it actually runs. The Xbox Series S is really pulling its weight. Just like I predicted in my last video, the XSS supports every feature of the game fully. It even has ray-traced hair strands, though there is a slight drop in detail and the image looks a little softer. If you don't have an enormous display, the XSS works perfectly fine. For just 1400 yuan, you can run this game. Rockstar's optimization is nothing short of incredible. The PS5 and Xbox Series X render at 1440P native, with absolutely stellar visuals. This is reportedly the best ray tracing. we've seen in any released game to date. Street environments are incredibly intricate, packed with countless dynamic assets, paired with atmospheric lighting that makes sunrises and sunsets look absolutely breathtaking. If you happen to own a PS5 Pro, congratulations: you're getting the best visual experience ever on a game console. The most powerful console paired with this flagship game delivers crisp, sharp imagery. You can make out skin textures on characters up close, building materials at mid-range, and crystal-clear water reflections. Rockstar says they have squeezed every last bit of performance out of the hardware.

Even when I'm just driving past streets for a mission or boating over to pick up a package, the roadside scenery keeps blowing me away. That said like many of you, I simply cannot stand playing at 30 FPS. I played the whole session with a capture card for frame interpolation. If you have an RTX 40-series or newer NVIDIA GPU, there's an open-source project that comes with frame generation and DLSS 5. It even has a beauty filter if you don't like how the protagonist looks, and the latency stays well within acceptable limits. GTA 6 has the richest detail of any game I've played. On your first playthrough, you will constantly be amazed by all the little touches. The map is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's,. with an astonishing density of detail. The storefronts along the streets feel authentic, and they are not copy-pasted; each one has unique decor and styling, just like the variety of boutique shops you'd find at a tourist spot. Sometimes when I pass a small shop, I genuinely get the urge to walk inside and look around. When you shop at a supermarket now, items no longer vanish into some alternate inventory pocket. You get a physical shopping bag instead. You have to place that bag in your car trunk, then carry the groceries up to your place once you get home. There's even an electronics store--my favorite kind of shop, can you believe it? They sell Beats headphones and phone cases. Hmm, though I wonder who's even going to see those phone cases. If you park in a tight spot, the protagonist will squeeze out sideways. Long guns no longer materialize out of thin air; they live inside a weapons case in the trunk. Pulling one out can attract unwanted attention, so you have to decide whether to carry that long rifle with you when you step out of the vehicle. Drinks you buy are held in either your left or right hand, and you have to set down each hand's items separately. I was blown away the first time I played San Andreas, back when characters could gain weight. Now the player character's physique. also changes based on your actions. Working out builds muscle and raises your health. Your in-game home even has its own game console not a PlayStation, it's called the JoySystem. And that zombie-shooting game on it? It's actually pretty fun. GTA 4 introduced the in-game cellphone, GTA 5 used phones to drive story beats, and in GTA 6, you can even browse a social media feed, check your fitness stats, and so much more. You can also use your phone while driving firing off texts or watching videos. It's one of those little details you really have to experience in GTA 6.

I've put in ten hours, and I've uncovered less than a tenth of the map. I can't even imagine how much more content is still ahead. I've run into hundreds of NPCs so far, and I haven't seen a duplicate. These aren't just procedurally generated mixes; Rockstar actually built tons of unique NPCs, each with their own personality it's insane. Take Jason, the male protagonist's neighbor, for example. You'll hear him every time you pull out of the driveway. Still, the NPC drivers left the biggest impression on me. The acceleration pushback feels so visceral. All I did was tap their car! You also run into all kinds of wild characters out on the road. Once I headed out to buy clothes, and right as I stepped outside, an elderly lady in a wheelchair tried to rob me. I kicked her, and she popped right back up. Total miracle worker, apparently. For driving in this entry, flooring the gas nonstop isn't recommended. If you're using a PlayStation controller, the throttle trigger has a distinct resistance notch. I usually hold the trigger right at that notch. You can also adjust the controller speaker volume in settings I'd recommend cranking it up. When you get an in-game call, the ringtone plays straight from the controller speaker, just like your real phone buzzing in your pocket. You can also route navigation audio to the controller. While driving, it feels like your phone is mounted up front, guiding you and alerting you once you reach your destination. And honestly, it's not just Americans complaining about high costs even I'm blown away by how expensive everything is. The protagonist risks life and limb, and a mission only pays around $300. Groceries and drinks for the family already run me $100. Adding a front bumper for a car modification costs hundreds more. The most absurd part? Toll roads. The electronic toll system charges me $5. Is this capitalism at work? A two-kilometer taxi ride costs $42. Rush the driver, and that's an extra $5. Skip the ride entirely, and they charge $100. Capitalists are even more ruthless than gangsters, if you ask me. Taxis in GTA 5 never cost this much per kilometer.

They even built inflation into the game. The cost of committing crimes has also gone up drastically. The protagonist almost behaves like a law-abiding citizen. Early on, you can't just hijack cars off the street willy-nilly. Your face, outfit and the vehicle you're driving will get flagged. Even if someone tries to rob you, you can't immediately take them out that will also trigger a wanted level. This might be the most rule-following GTA yet. That said, Rockstar stated they wanted to balance gameplay fun and realism. Take Joey, the auto shop guy from Lantos Reef, the strongest NPC in the whole game. He can teleport your car to you for free. A true good samaritan of Vice City. The localization is also wild. The bank the female protagonist robs is called Get Cash Now. Lots of games have scan mechanics, but what on earth is "AI Snoop"? When the protagonist first sets up the family fund, the banking app they hand their cash over to has a very specific name you'll know it if you get the reference. I cracked up when the male lead and his best friend had a whole conversation about feng shui. And get this: the radio even includes Cantonese tracks. Would you believe it? That said, the story just doesn't deliver the same chaotic, liberating rush I got from GTA 5. The pacing is extremely slow-burn. The first ten hours are basically just the two leads playing house and falling in love. Even now, I haven't met a single character that sticks with me. After all this playtime, I still can't pin down the male protagonist's personality all I know is he's head over heels for the female lead. The game doesn't spend much time explaining why, either. If you ask what kind of GTA story I want? Give me something like: the protagonist's wife is cheating with a personal trainer, so he storms over to wreck the trainer's place only to find he's just ransacked a crime boss's home. Or open with the protagonist being an absolute menace,. and within a minute, he stomps the skull of a returning character from the previous game. Think about it: for a regular game, more than half the players would have dropped out by this point. The only thing keeping me going right now is the urge to keep exploring this open world. Also, the classic cheat codes everyone loves are only unlocked after beating the game. Next up, let's break down how each console performs in detail. The Xbox Series S really exceeded my expectations. At its price point, it makes zero major compromises to hair rendering or NPC population density. It renders at 720P and upscales to 1080P. It does look a little soft on a TV, but I think the full experience.

holds up perfectly well on a 24–27 inch monitor. There are a few downgrades in finer details, though. Reflections on puddles and glass panes are simplified. When NPCs walk past, you can get these ghosting artifacts. Character skin textures are also scaled back; clothing is basically baked onto the model and won't blow in the wind. Rockstar cut quite a few visual features to preserve a baseline playable experience on the Series S, and somehow they got this next-gen title running on hardware that's closer to the last generation. We'll cover the Xbox Series X and PS5 together, as their performance is fairly similar. Both render at 1440P and handle ray-traced reflections in much the same way. I've covered the logos here can you guess which console is which? One small but important detail: VRR on the PS5 only activates above 48 FPS, and the game is locked to 30 FPS, so VRR does not function during normal gameplay. The Series X, however, supports VRR, which keeps things looking smoother during frame drops. If you're stuck. choosing between the Series X and PS5, here's my breakdown. If visual presentation is your priority, go with the Series X. It has slightly stronger hardware, more stable frame pacing, plus VRR to prevent screen tearing when frames dip. The overall image feels more consistent and smooth. It also supports Dolby Vision the Series X is built to nail visual output. If gameplay feel matters most to you, pick the PS5 without hesitation. The DualSense haptics. are in a completely different league from Xbox controllers. You feel distinct feedback over different road surfaces: gravel gives this messy, rumbling vibration, while asphalt delivers subtle, steady tremors, just like holding a real steering wheel. Even tapping confirm or back on the in-game phone triggers a tiny vibration mimicking the phone's motor. It's absurdly immersive. Now for the top-tier PS5 Pro. I'm sure you've all seen that meme going around. Honestly, it's not like that at all. It's still locked at 30 FPS, but the visual quality is on another level. Its exclusive PSSR upscaling pulls its weight.

Compared with every other console, material resolution on surfaces is higher, and jagged edges are far less noticeable. On top of that, the PS5 Pro gets exclusive ray-traced shadows. Shadows cast by lighting are sharper and far more true to real life. This is easily the best-looking AAA game out there. If we push it even further and run the captured footage through DLSS 5 on top of that… the visuals would be unreal. GTA 6 truly stands as one of the greatest video games of this era. With AAA development costs skyrocketing, this might genuinely be the swan song for games of this scale. Thirteen years passed between GTA 5 and GTA 6, and it's very possible we won't see a production this ambitious for another decade. It's weirdly a little bit sad, right after launch. I love the GTA series not just because it gives us this massive open-world playground. Every prior entry also had incredibly compelling protagonist stories. My favorite character in the whole franchise is Trevor. I even saw a clip once at a GTA booth where someone asked him, "Trevor, can you insult me?" Whenever I think of GTA 5, I picture that over-the-top, bizarre, sarcastic story. I wonder if GTA 6 can give me that same feeling. Alright, that wraps up this video.
